# The harnesses

Generated 2026-11-10 by `ham.citybuildersim.tools.HarnessMap` - every labelled assertion in every harness, under the section it prints. Do not edit; regenerate with `Regenerate maps.bat`.

**195 harness files, 23,003 labelled assertions.** AllChecks runs 195 of them.

## AgricultureCheck.java - 48 labelled assertions

> The ground under the loaf.
> 
> WHAT THIS HAS TO PROVE. Not that the city got bigger - it did not, and the
> measurement is in claude/farms.md where a number that will drift belongs.
> What is checkable is whether the tenth sector does the four things it was
> built to do:
> 
>   1. the mills BUY their raw material now, and the chain is four links deep
>   2. crops clear in a band with a real import ceiling, so a city with no
>      fields eats anyway and pays for the privilege
>   3. a farm is ground and almost nothing else - and the clock that runs on
>      that ground is what decides fields against glass
> ...

- **L78 1. the good, and the chain it closes**
  - L81 crops can be imported - a city with no fields still eats
  - L83 ...and exported, so a farming city can ship its surplus
  - L85 ...and stored, because a harvest keeps and that is what a silo is
  - L87 crops clear on the band
  - L88 a tonne costs more to bring in than a farm gets shipping one out
  - L90 crops are sold by the tonne
  - L101 the Industrial Bakery buys crops, which it never did before
  - L103 ...and so does the Bakery
  - L114 a tonne of crops comes out as 52.5% of its own mass, baked, at the big oven
  - L117 ...and at the small one
  - L131 the mills declare crops as an input on the sector, not just the template
  - L133 ...and the fields declare them as an output
- **L169 2. the band, and the city with no fields**
  - L174 nobody growing any - the mills pay what the world charges
  - L177 nobody buying any - the fields get what the ship pays
  - L180 ...and a matched pair splits the difference
- **L185 3. a farm is ground and almost nothing else**
  - L239 a field takes more ground a post than any factory in the game
  - L249 ...and far more ground per dollar of harvest than glass does
  - L252 glass pays for its density in power
  - L255 a field's wage bill is small against what it sells
  - L275 dear ground makes a field cost many times what glass costs
  - L277 ...while the glass is still mostly the glass
- **L279 4. the dial, and what reads it**
  - L282 full relief by default, which is what real jurisdictions do
  - L305 six grain farms is 3,000 tonnes of crop a month
  - L307 the fields sold something
  - L308 the mills bought crops
  - L309 ...from the fields, at home
  - L310 ...and the fields' own crop line shows it
  - L322 the fields are standing on real money
  - L334 full relief takes the ground off the roll and leaves the barns
  - L336 no relief puts all of it back
  - L337 and it touches nobody else's assessment
  - L339 the share on the roll is one for everybody else
  - L342 ...and one less the relief for the fields
  - L345 the dial cannot be set past full relief
  - L347 ...nor below none
  - L358 the bill the fields are actually charged follows the dial
  - L366 the investment desk prices a prospective farm at the relieved rate too
- **L370 and nobody breaks ground while somebody sleeps outside**
  - L373 the sector answers with a reason either way
  - L377 Agriculture is the tenth sector
  - L379 ...and the share register is the sectors and the bank
  - L386 a reloaded city has the same fields
  - L389 ...the same cash
  - L392 ...and the same farmland dial, which is a policy and has to survive
- **L395 5. a farm is counted in the money the measure counts in (RT1)**
  - L415 fixture: every good the fields make has an export floor above nothing, so each is in the measure
  - L417 ...and the fields hold two kinds of farm, the Grain Farm the more, so it is the one the rule would thin
  - L428 a farm is counted in the measure's own unit: what the farms add up to is the capacity the measure reports
  - L435 ...so, losing money RETIREMENT_LOSS_MONTHS months with nothing used, the rule sells the most-held kind of farm
  - L439 ...at the founding's price level, where a money-per-tonne quotient sold nothing (PriceLevel.FACTOR below 1)

## ArrivalMixCheck.java - 44 labelled assertions

> The skill mix of the arrivals by year (R0d slice 2): the year's mix in a city founded the 1900 way, and WageBand's ceilings in every
> other city. Not part of the game.
> 
> WHAT THIS HAS TO PROVE (R0d, 2026-11-06; docs/studies/research-1900.md 5.4 item 6 and 12.1, "Skill mix by year"). A 1901 arrival was a
> labourer or a farm hand far more often than a diploma-holder, and a graduate was rare; the mix reaches today's by 2021, and only a city
> founded the 1900 way is drawn from it. What is checkable:
> 
>   1. THE KNOTS: in year order, each one's shares non-negative and summing to one, a source key or the estimate flag on each, the last
>      one today's model, and the mix from its January on today's constants themselves
>   2. THE LOOK-UP: a knot's own point at its January, the mean of two knots' shares half-way, the first knot's before the first, the
>      university figure never falling and the no-diploma one never rising from month to month, the same month the same point
>   3. AGAINST THE STUDY: a 1901 arrival at the going rate most likely holds no diploma, and 1953's university share is a good
> ...

- **L112 1. the knots: in year order, shares summing to one, a source or an estimate flag, the last one today's model**
  - L114 the table has knots, from the 1900s on
  - L131 the last knot is today's model: no ordinary arrivals without a diploma (derived)
  - L133 ...its college figure is WageBand's ceiling (derived)
  - L134 ...its university figure is WageBand's ceiling (derived)
  - L135 today's mix is WageBand's own ceilings, with nothing arriving without a diploma at the going rate
  - L145 from the last knot's January and for 1,200 months after it the mix is TODAY itself, not a derived copy
- **L151 2. the look-up: a knot's own point at its January, the mean of two knots half-way, the first before the first**
  - L163 ...the college figure
  - L164 ...the university figure
  - L170 before the first knot's January the first knot's mix applies, down to a month the calendar floors
  - L189 every month from the first knot's January to the last's is a finite non-negative mix
  - L190 the university figure never falls, month by month, from 1901 to 2021
  - L191 ...nor does the college figure
  - L192 ...and the arrivals without a diploma at the going rate (per diploma arrival) never rise
  - L193 two calls for the same month give the same point, the mix having no state
  - L194 ...and the mix has moved: 1901 has more ordinary arrivals without a diploma than 2021, and fewer university graduates
- **L202 3. against the study (research-1900 5.4): 1901's arrival most likely holds no diploma, and 1953 has several times the graduates**
  - L204 a 1901 arrival is most likely without a diploma: the 1901 knot's no-diploma share is above a half
  - L206 ...so at the going rate the arrivals without a diploma outnumber the diploma-holders, where today's model has none of them
  - L209 1953's university share is at least 2.5 times 1901's (the study: 1.2 students per 1,000 in 1901, 4.7 in 1950)
  - L210 ...and 1953's working arrivals hold more diplomas, college degrees and university degrees than 1901's, and fewer of them none
- **L268 4. Migration on the year's mix: today's mix is today's model; 1913 at the going rate is mostly undiplomaed; 1953 brings more graduates wh...**
  - L275 fixture: at base no band is dear: the premium of every band is the going rate
  - L276 fixture: bid up, the college and university bands are bought for more than a third of their ceilings
  - L284 fixture: people arrive into the city the draw is made in
  - L297 fixture: bid up, graduates and licence-holders arrive in today's model (so the join below compares something)
  - L300 the arrivals by band and the licences are the same with no mix as with TODAY, at the going rate and bid up, to 1e-12
  - L302 ...and how many arrive is the same: the volume is not the mix's
  - L307 1913 at the going rate: no college graduate arrives
  - L308 ...no university graduate, and no licence-holder
  - L310 ...and the arrivals without a diploma outnumber the diploma-holders
  - L311 ...by the year's figure: no-diploma arrivals per diploma arrival
  - L312 ...everyone who arrives is placed once: the bands sum to the month's arrivals
  - L313 ...where today's model brings nobody without a diploma at the going rate, and 1913's brings the same number of people
  - L321 fixture: bid up, 1913 brings some graduates
  - L322 with the graduate bands bid up, 1953 brings a larger share of graduates than 1913
  - L324 ...and today's model, the last mix, a larger share still
  - L325 ...with the arrivals without a diploma a smaller share of 1953's than of 1913's, bid up
- **L332 5. played: a city founded the 1900 way draws on the year's mix every month for 24, a default city on none**
  - L335 fixture: one village founded the 1900 way, the other the default way
  - L336 a new city holds no mix before its first month
  - L364 24 months played: the clock moved one month a press
  - L365 ...each month the 1900 city's Migration holds the year's mix, ArrivalMix.at() of the month played
  - L366 fixture: people arrived in the 1900 city over the 24 months
  - L367 ...its arrivals by band sum to the month's arrivals, every month
  - L369 ...and over the 24 months more arrive without a diploma than with one
  - L370 a city founded the default way holds no mix in any of its 24 months
  - L371 ...and the same village founded the default way draws a smaller share of its arrivals without a diploma

## AuctionCheck.java - 298 labelled assertions

> The city's paper sold at auction: one clearing yield, and what it costs.
> 
> WHAT THIS HAS TO PROVE (spec-city-debt.md, section 4; CD2). Auction is pure -
> a snapshot of the bidders and the ask in, a result out - so sections 1 to 6
> start no Game:
> 
>   1. EACH BIDDER BIDS BY THE RULE IT ALREADY FOLLOWS, against that rule's own
>      constants: the households' (D32) out of savings and never past the
>      issue, the firms' (D33) as OutwardInvestment moves their money, the
>      world's as CapitalFlows.stockAt() sizes its stock, the bank's room at
>      fair and nothing under.
> 
> ...

- **L241 1. each bidder's rule against its constants**
  - L247 households a point over deposits take appetite x spread x face
  - L250 ...which at the study's fair yield is its table's D$126.1M
  - L254 a spread wide enough to want twice the issue is capped at the issue
  - L259 D32: a spread that wants four fifths of the issue gets four fifths
  - L260 ...which is more than the old half-the-issue cap would have let through
  - L265 thin savings cap them at savings past the cushion, whatever the spread
  - L267 ...and at a modest spread too, where the rule would take more than they have
  - L270 at the deposit rate they take nothing
  - L271 under the deposit rate they take nothing
  - L274 a negative deposit rate is read as zero: the spread is the yield itself
  - L282 firms a point over the better of deposit and world: target share of idle money, at OUT_SPEED
  - L284 ...the target being APPETITE x the spread of their idle money, a point under MAX_SHARE
  - L288 at the world's rate (the better of the two) they bid nothing
  - L289 under it they bid nothing

> The railway's carriage of the city's own bulk, and the port yard, held to FR6's
> brief: a bulk tonne bought at home rides a siding at the city leg's rate on
> the room the boundary's tonnes leave, a tonne that crossed a berth rides the
> port yard's rails to the same rule, and every leg is billed once.
> 
> WHY THIS HARNESS EXISTS. Until FR6 the railway was offered only what crossed
> the boundary: the ore from a city's mine to its own mill was a whole truck leg
> at Haulage's quote though FR7 lays the mine a siding, and a tonne landed at a
> berth was a whole truck leg from the quay to the door. FR6 (docs/queue/FR6.md)
> deals those tonnes to the railway last, after the boundary's, bills them at the
> railway's quote on Haulage's, and takes their railed part off the trucks' leg.

> ...

> The Hydro Station and the river it needs (HY1, 2026-10-26; docs/queue/HY1-notes.md): the physics of a drop against

> that orders up to its slots, and the real Earth's rivers when earth-2.bin is named. Not part of the game.
>

> plot at its relief class's least grade, with the flow from the river's width. Every rule of that reading is caused

> Earth is asked only whether a river of the real world reads as one: a hydro town does, a flat one does not.

## KeptCheck.java - 422 labelled assertions

> The People page kept between redraws (study UP4, docs/studies/spec-screens-in-place.md): each
> month's redraw run over last month's nodes ends exactly where a page built new would, and costs
> a fraction of it.
> 
> WHY THIS EXISTS. A kept page (ui.Kept) runs the screen's own drawing code every month over the
> nodes it made the month before. What can go wrong is what a node carries from one month into the
> next: a value set under a condition that no longer holds, a list added to, a listener added
> twice, a picture told only half its new figures. None of it shows on the month it is written;
> all of it shows as a page that is not the page the city would draw. So this draws the page both
> ways at every month of a played stretch and compares them - every node's words, style, the
> values code set, handlers, tooltip and place, and at some months every pixel - and only then
> times the kept month.
> ...

## PriceLevelCheck.java - 69 labelled assertions

> A city founded at 1900's prices is today's real economy with every dollar multiplied by one factor, and this is how we know (EP1, Jerus
> 2026-10-30: "1900 price level"; docs/studies/spec-1900-start.md 2).
> 
> WHY. The calendar starts in 1900 with today's technology, and "1900 price level" means every nominal anchor - the world's prices, the wage
> rungs, the building costs, the opening money, every dollar dial - is today's figure times PriceLevel.FACTOR (the US CPI of 1900 over 2025,
> 0.02588) and no ratio, rate, count or physical quantity moves. The anchors are in over a hundred places and a missed one is not an error: it
> is a relative price that is silently off by 38.6 times, so food costs a labourer's day or a house costs a week's pay, and nobody sees it
> until a screen reads strange. Nobody can enumerate this codebase's money by reading it, so the test is not a list of fields: it is TWO CITIES,
> as DenominationCheck's is.
> 
>   A is founded at the factor, as the game is.
>   B is founded at today's prices (-Dcbs.priceLevel=1, PriceLevel's one door).

## PrizeCheck.java - 214 labelled assertions

> A prize pays only for a result, a Research Lab goes for the cheapest problem the purse pays for, and the schools' share of a purse buys posts
> (R4, slice A: Research; docs/studies/research-design.md 5.3, 1.5, 5.4).
> 
> WHY. A grant pays for the work whether it finds anything or not; a prize pays only for the find, and the whole point of it (5.3) is WHO does the
> work: labs do not spread as the city's researchers do, they go for the cheapest problem a team could finish before the world, and the
> purse is split by who did the work. Every claim here is a statement about a month and a threshold ("the prize is at least the remaining work
> times a researcher-year's cost": one hair under it a lab stays away), so each threshold is caused from both sides and held to Research's own
> constants and functions and never to a number copied from the study's formula; and a wrong order in the month (the chase computed after the
> work, the purse read before the find) moves a find by a year and no assertion elsewhere would see it. Sections 1 to 10 (slice A) are the
> pure model, which has to be right before Game meets it; sections 11 to 17 (slice B) are Game meeting it.
> 
> What this has to prove:
> ...

> Reading the city must not change the city.
> 
> WHY THIS EXISTS
> 
> Three of the worst bugs this project has had were the same bug:

## ResearchPreviewCheck.java - 82 labelled assertions

> The preview each dial card on Policy > Research shows: what a set of dials would find here over ten years (R3b, slice A: ResearchPreview, and the
> words and the cache in ResearchView; docs/studies/research-design.md 5.4, 6.2, 9).
> 
> WHY. The preview is the one place the game says a number about the FUTURE of a random process, and its numbers are the player's reason to move a
> dial. A step that differs from the game's own by one rule (the labs read the city's share of this month and not the last, a find not counting at once
> for the fields after it) would give a card that promises what the month will not deliver, and no other assertion in the model would see it; and a
> sampler that leaked the city's own draw would show the player a size they are not to see. So: the two cities of research-design 5.4 are held to the
> study's figures, which research_model.py made with the study's own model, within their Monte Carlo error; the preview's step is held to
> Research.month() itself, month for month, over given sizes; the answer is the same for the same inputs and is never run twice for them; and the
> words are caused from both sides of each edge.
>

> ...

> WHY. The screens draw only what the model hands them, and a wrong month in the timeline, a piece shown before it is known, or a NEW mark one month

> its screens). The cores that take a catalogue, a research and a month are driven at any month with a research of their own, and the Game-level reads

## SaveFileCheck.java - 699 labelled assertions

> Verifies where saves go and how they are written.
> 
> This is the only part of the game where a bug destroys something the player
> cannot get back. Everything else can be re-simulated; a save written over
> badly is a city that no longer exists. So the tests here are deliberately
> mean: they fill the target with junk, point the writer at a path it cannot
> write to, and check that in every case the file that was already on disk is
> still exactly what it was.
> 
> Path resolution is tested through the pure resolveDirectory() rather than the
> real environment, because a chooser that reads System.getenv can only be
> tested on the machine it is running on - which is precisely the machine where
> ...

## SaveSlotCheck.java - 202 labelled assertions

> Verifies the slot system: ten saves plus an autosave, the version stamp, and
> the labels the menu is drawn from.
> 
> The thing this is really guarding is INDEPENDENCE. A save menu that shows ten
> slots and quietly writes them all to the same file, or draws slot 3's label
> from slot 7's city, is worse than a single save - it invites a player to
> spread a hundred hours across ten slots that were never really there.
> 
> AND THE AUTOSAVE HOLDS A WHOLE MONTH (0.7.52). Until 0.7.51 the twelfth
> month's autosave was written near the top of Game.nextMonth(), after the
> calendar had turned and before the month ran: the file said month N, its
> history ended at N - 1, and a city loaded from it never ran N. Each of the
> ...
